content: Use a compact prompt contract instead of a vague request: state the goal, relevant context or assets, hard constraints, preferred output format, and any known failure modes. This makes prompt revisions easier to compare across image, video, and digital-human providers.
summary: State goal, context/assets, constraints, output format, and failure modes as a compact prompt contract.

rules.text: Separate intent, context/assets, constraints, and output format before adding style details.

content: Delimit reference material from instructions. For Prompt Agent use, name each asset/reference explicitly and keep the requested transformation separate from raw script, storyboard, product facts, or previous prompt text.
summary: Use delimiters and labels so reference material is not mistaken for instructions.

rules.text: Label each reference block by role, then write the actual instruction after the references.

content: Examples are useful only when they match the target task and format. A text-only example can mislead an image/video rewrite; prefer short examples that demonstrate asset roles, camera/motion fields, negative constraints, or JSON output shape.
summary: Keep examples short and matched to the target media prompt format.

rules.text: Use examples to show the desired structure, not to smuggle unrelated style or content into the prompt.

content: Split complex prompt work into smaller decisions: first identify objective and assets, then choose composition/camera, then describe motion or transformation, then add negatives and output requirements. This maps well to image and video prompt critique workflows.
summary: Break complex media prompts into objective, assets, composition, motion, negatives, and output requirements.

rules.text: Decompose a complex rewrite before producing the final prompt, especially when assets, camera, and motion all matter.

content: When another service will consume the result, ask for a predictable schema. For digital human workflows, keep avatar, voice, script, motion, captions, and output settings as separate fields instead of merging them into one prose prompt.
summary: Use structured fields when prompts feed downstream tools or APIs.

rules.text: Return downstream-facing prompt data as explicit fields, not a single paragraph, when the API has separate controls.

content: Treat prompt writing as an iterative test loop. Record what changed, why it changed, and which artifact or failure it is addressing so future Prompt Agent searches can retrieve lessons from local experience.
summary: Track prompt iterations by changed rule, target artifact, and observed failure.

rules.text: Keep prompt revisions attributable to a concrete failure or improvement target.

content: Negative constraints should target known failure modes, not become a long generic blacklist. For visual/video prompts, pair each negative with a positive desired constraint when possible, such as stable camera, clean frame, or no extra text because captions are handled elsewhere.
summary: Use negatives for specific failure modes and pair them with positive constraints.

rules.text: Avoid long generic negative lists that do not correspond to the actual provider or asset failure mode.

content: Keep prompts focused on controllable variables. Remove motivational phrasing, generic quality adjectives, or broad background theory when the user needs a provider-ready image, video, lipsync, or avatar prompt.
summary: Remove broad theory and generic praise; keep controllable prompt variables.

rules.text: Avoid letting general prompt-engineering advice crowd out concrete media controls such as asset role, camera, motion, script, and output format.
